column2: meaning (the names are census keys where the census has one; the refusals of corpus/manifest and of the testkit fixtures use only these)
The file is an OLE compound file, which is how Word stores an encrypted or password-protected .docx, and not a ZIP archive.
The file is not a ZIP archive: it is empty or does not start like one.
There is no end of central directory record, so the archive is cut short or is not a ZIP archive.
The end of central directory record is cut short.
The comment length in the end record is larger than the bytes that follow it.
The end record points at a central directory that is not in the file.
The central directory is shorter than the end record says.
The entry count in the end record differs from the number of records in the central directory.
A central directory record points at an offset where there is no local file header.
The central directory is not where the end record says it is.
Entries overlap or are not in increasing offset order, so two entries can share bytes.
The central directory overlaps the data of an entry.
A local header names an entry differently from the central directory, so readers disagree about which part it is.
A local header and the central directory give different compression methods for one entry, so readers decode different bytes.
A local header and the central directory give different CRC-32 values or sizes for one entry.
An entry name contains a `..` segment, the path traversal pattern.
An entry name contains a `.` segment, so two spellings name the same part.
An entry name contains an empty segment, such as a double slash.
An entry name is absolute or starts with a drive letter.
An entry name contains a backslash.
An entry name contains a NUL byte.
An entry name contains a control character.
An entry name is longer than 255 bytes; a ZIP name field holds up to 65,535.
Two entries have the same name, so readers disagree about which one is the part.
Two entries have names that differ only by case, and part names are case-insensitive.
The archive has 10,000 or more entries.
An entry declares an uncompressed size of 256 MB or more.
An entry declares an uncompressed size above the limit.

Bytes lie between two entries, or between the last entry and the central directory, that belong to no entry. A reader that goes through the file in order sees what is in them, and a reader that goes by the central directory does not, so a hidden entry shows in one and not the other.

The bytes in front of the first entry start like a ZIP file: the file is one archive followed by another. The readers that look for the end record read the second, and a reader that goes through the file from the front reads the first.

A ZIP64 locator precedes the end record and leads to a ZIP64 end record whose entry count, directory size or directory offset differs from the end record's. The readers that follow the ZIP64 record and the ones that use the end record read different archives.
An entry's recorded compressed size runs past the end of the file.
The end record names a disk other than the first, so the archive is split over several files.
A data descriptor is not where the entry sizes put it.
The CRC-32 of an entry differs from the one recorded.
The deflate stream of an entry is invalid.
An entry inflates to a size other than the declared one.
An entry has the encrypted flag set.
An entry uses compression method 99 (AES encryption), which stetdoc does not support.
An entry uses compression method 12 (bzip2), which stetdoc does not support.
An entry uses compression method 14 (LZMA), which stetdoc does not support.
A stored entry records a size that differs from the bytes it holds.
An entry compresses far better than text does, which is the shape of a decompression bomb.
The XML nests 100 levels or more.
An element has 50 or more attributes.
The part has a DOCTYPE declaration, which OOXML parts do not use.
The DOCTYPE declares entities, the starting point of entity expansion and external entity attacks.
The DOCTYPE names an external DTD, which must never be fetched.
The DOCTYPE has an internal subset.
An ampersand that does not start a reference, which is not well-formed XML.
A reference to an entity that XML does not define, such as the HTML entity for a non-breaking space.
A numeric character reference to a code point that XML forbids.
The XML declaration gives a version other than 1.0, and OOXML parts are XML 1.0.
The declared encoding does not match the bytes of the part.
The declaration names an encoding that is neither UTF-8 nor UTF-16, and OPC allows only those two.
The part contains characters that XML 1.0 forbids.
The part contains bytes that are not valid in its encoding.
Start tags and end tags do not balance.
Text or markup comes before the root element.
Content follows the root element.
An element repeats an attribute.
An attribute value contains a literal `<`, which XML forbids.
An attribute value has no closing quote.
The text of an element contains `]]>`, which XML allows only at the end of a CDATA section; a `>` after `]]` is written `>`.
A comment is opened and never closed.
A comment contains `--`, which XML 1.0 forbids but which changes no structure.
The part has no root element.
A name uses a namespace prefix that is not declared.
A part the package needs is not well-formed XML.
The archive has no [Content_Types].xml, so it is not an OPC package.
The archive has no _rels/.rels, so nothing says which part is the main document.
The root relationship names a main document part that is not in the package.
The root relationship names a main part that is in the package but is not a WordprocessingML document: its content type is something else, such as a theme manager or a spreadsheet.
A relationship target walks above the package root. The package opens and the target is never resolved outside it.
A part is itself a ZIP archive. It is an opaque part and is never opened.
